bargein._note: Measured as cessation of audio_out frames on the wire — closer to the spec's acoustic requirement than the software cancel event, but NOT a microphone recording of the speaker; client-side buffer drain is excluded.
bargein._measurement_caveat: Measured from the ONSET of injected user speech to the last audio_out frame, matching the spec definition. It therefore includes VAD lead-in (~160 ms of sustained speech is required before barge-in triggers) and is NOT a pure interrupt-to-silence figure. n=8, far below the spec-s 50 trials.

i1_checker.reason: The voice WebSocket emits the grounded answer as token-level streaming deltas ("The" -> "The liability" -> "The liability cap"...). The harness counted each delta as a distinct L_I utterance and scored it as a novel assertion preceding its increment, producing a spurious 0.111 violation rate over 1357 pseudo-utterances. Separating L_I (lead phrase) from L_G (grounded stream) requires event-level provenance the protocol does not currently carry. Reported as not_measurable rather than as a number.
i1_checker.what_would_fix_it: tag each assistant_phrase/assistant_text_partial event with its originating loop (L_I vs L_G) in voice/app/session.py, then re-run.

_limitations: n=12 turns, below the spec's >=200 utterances / >=50 barge-in trials.
Barge-in measured on the wire, not from a recorded speaker waveform.
